summary: Iteration 76 review of ScoutMePlay conversion package. All 7 backend pytest cases pass (public /api/demo-report, /api/admin/email-log auth/data, public open pixel, /api/reports auth regression, conversion-sweep dry-run schema, and — most critically — verified NO full_report leak in GET /api/reports/{id} for a non-paying user). All frontend flows pass: landing '/' hero CTA links to /sample-report; DemoReportPage renders all 4 testids (demo-report-banner, demo-report-upload-cta, demo-report-bottom-cta, demo-report-bottom-upload) with the full Noah sample report body; Admin > Email tab shows the Sent-log block (had to click 'Show' to expand — worked) with all 3 stat/search testids plus 4 email-log-row-{id} rows and one green '✓ opened' timestamp on the activation email; FreePreviewLanding renders 30 fpl-* testids including fpl-locked-sections + 10 blurred fpl-locked-section-{i} rows + fpl-locked-sections-unlock + fpl-locked-sections-sample (href='/sample-report'); Admin > Growth sweep-dry-btn hits POST /api/admin/conversion-sweep?dry_run=true and returns JSON with both 'results' and 'activation' keys. Landing has 0 console errors. All seeded test data cleaned up; email_log entries preserved.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 14k+ lines — main agent already flagged; splitting into routers (reports, admin, growth, email) would help maintenance but not urgent.

The email-log Sent-log block defaults to collapsed with a 'Show' toggle — testids only render after expand; UI test scripts must click Show first. Consider defaulting to open for admins so the log is visible at a glance.

Because the paywall pytest signup created a real user with a fresh signup, a 'Welcome' welcome email was auto-sent to paywalltest_*@example.com (visible in email_log as the 4th row). Not a leak (test-created address only), but signup path fires a broadcast even for @example.com addresses. If activation sweep already skips @example.com, consider also skipping the initial welcome for @example.com to keep the log fully clean during testing.
